title: 3D Microtissues for Injectable Regenerative Therapy and High-throughput Drug Screening
protocol: Use commercial software to design arrays of specific geometries depending on subsequent application.
Import the design into the laser engraving software accompanying the laser engraving machine.
Laser-engrave the imported design onto Poly (methymethacrylate) (PMMA) sheets using factory recommended settings for the laser engraving machine.
Wash microstencil array chips with deionized water to clean debris from the laser engraving.
Dry the microstencil array chips at 60 °C.
Store dried microstencil array chips in a sealed bag at room temperature.
Place 4 microstencil array chips on the sample tray.
Insert the sample tray into the plasma cleaner.
Close the door of the plasma cleaner.
Turn on the vacuum pump for 2 min.
Turn on the maximum RF power (18 W) to treat the microstencil array chips in the plasma cleaner for 3 min at room temperature.
Add 0.06 g gelatin to 1 mL deionized water to form a 6% (wt/vol) gelatin precursor solution.
Warm the gelatin precursor solution at 60 °C in a water bath until dissolved adequately.
Incubate the solution on ice for 5 min.
Add 3 µL of glutaraldehyde into the gelatin precursor solution to achieve a final concentration of 0.3%.
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Pipette 200 µL of the precursor solution with glutaraldehyde onto the upper surface of each microstencil array chip.
Manually distribute the solution evenly over the chip by scraping back and forth with a bent glass rod 2 to 3 times.
Place the precursor-solution-filled array chips in a -20 °C freezer for 16 h for cryogelation.
Adjust the lyophilizer to -40 °C for 30 min.
Place the array chips after cryogelation in the lyophilizer.
Lyophilize the array chips for 2 h under vacuum.
Design arrays of 600 circles, each with a diameter of 400 µm, in commercial software for injectable 3D microtissue construction.
Fabricate a PDMS Ejector Pin array using standard soft lithography.
Overlay the microcryogel array chip on top of the PDMS Ejector Pin array, aligning each microcryogel with an ejector pin on the array.
Press the microcryogel array chip towards the PDMS Ejector Pin array to push the microcryogels out of the microwells.
Harvest individual microcryogels into water using cell strainers.
Wash microcryogels with 0.1 M NaBH4 on ice for 20 min.
Discard NaBH4 and wash with 5 mL deionized water three to five times, 15 minutes each time.
Gather microcryogels into one cluster per cell strainer.
Place one cluster in a 35-mm Petri dish using a curved tweezer.
Add 50 - 70 µL deionized water to each cluster and cover the lid of the Petri dish.
Tap the Petri dish gently on the tabletop to level out all microcryogels.
Freeze harvested microcryogels at -20 °C for 4 to 16 hours before lyophilizing them for 2 hours.
Store microcryogels in a vacuum at room temperature until further use.
Immobilize harvested and lyophilized microcryogels onto a sample holder by double-side adhesive tape.
Coat the immobilized microcryogels with gold using a sputter coater for 90 seconds.
Image coated microcryogels by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Evaluate and analyze the distribution of diameters of pores in the microcryogel from seven different SEM images using image analysis software.
Weigh one cluster of 600 lyophilized microcryogels in a 35-mm Petri dish.
Add 60 μL deionized water to the cluster of lyophilized microcryogels.
Wait for 30 seconds for the microcryogels to fully absorb water and swell.
Weigh the swollen microcryogels.
Determine the equilibrium swelling ratio as the ratio of weight of swollen microcryogels to that of dried gelatin microcryogels.
Determine the porosity as the ratio of weight of held water in microcryogels to that of hydrated microcryogels.
Measure injectability using a programmable syringe pump integrated with a digital force gauge.
Stain 600 pieces of microcryogels by Trypan blue.
Suspend stained microcryogels in 600 μL 15% gelatin solution for homogeneous distribution.
Load 1 mL microcryogel suspension into a 1 mL syringe.
Attach a 27-gauge needle to the 1 mL syringe.
Inject the mixture through the needle using a programmable syringe pump at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Monitor real-time injection force by digital force gauge testing.
Plot the force-time curve.
Observe the integrity of microcryogels under a microscope after injection.
Measure the weight of one cluster of 600 lyophilized microcryogels in a 35-mm Petri dish as the dry weight.
Immerse 600 lyophilized microcryogels in 2 mL 0.025% (vol/vol) Trypsin/EDTA solution.
Collect microcryogels from the solution using a cell strainer at different time points (i.e., 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70 min).
Wick away excess solution with a tissue.
Measure the weight of microcryogels at each time point.
Calculate the degradation degree as the ratio of the weight of microcryogel at a certain time point to that at time zero.
Sterilize microcryogels from step 2.1.8 by ethylene oxide sterilization system with 12 h gas exposure followed by 12 h degassing under vacuum.
Choose human adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs) for treatment of mouse ischemic hindlimb.
Isolate cells by following previously reported procedures.

Culture hMSCs in the growth medium containing 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 10 ng/mL epidermal growth factor (EGF), 10 ng/mL platelet-derived growth factor bb (PDGF-bb), 1X insulin transferrin selenium (ITS), 10-8 M dexamethasone, 10-4 M ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 µg/mL streptomycin in DMEM/F12.
Passage the cells at a ratio of 1:3 when confluent.
Use cells of passage 3 to 5 for following experiments.
Harvest hMSCs with trypsin.
Quantify the cell number using a Fuchs-Rosenthal counting chamber.
Resuspend cells to a density of 8 x 10^6 cells/mL in hMSC growth medium.
Pipette 60 µL hMSC suspension onto the monolayer of 600 microcryogels with a diameter of 400 µm in a 35-mm dish.
Incubate at 37 °C for 2 hours to allow cells to attach.
Add 2 mL culture medium after 2 hours of incubation.
Change the medium every 2 days.
Culture hMSCs-loaded microcryogels for 2 days to form 3D microtissues.
Pipette 100 hMSCs-loaded microcryogels per well on a 96-well plate.
Add 120 µL of resazurin working solution into each well according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C.
Detect fluorescence of resazurin metabolized by viable cells in a microplate reader with an excitation light wavelength of 560 nm and emission light wavelength of 590 nm.
Stain cells in microcryogels with 1:500 dilution of Calcein AM and 1:250 dilution of Propidium Iodide in phosphate buffered saline.
Observe stained cells under fluorescence microscope or confocal fluorescence microscope.
Establish critical hindlimb ischemia of female BALB/c nude mice as reported to determine the therapeutic effect of 3D microtissue-based therapy.
Transfer hMSCs-loaded 3D microtissues from step 2.3.6 using a 5-mL pipette into a cell strainer and filter away the culture medium.
Resuspend the filtered microtissues in 15% gelatin solution at a density of 100 microcryogels per 100 µL solution.
Sterilize surgical tools by autoclave before surgery.
Place mouse into anesthesia induction chamber containing 1-3% isoflurane in 100% oxygen at a flow rate of 1 L/min.
Apply erythromycin on the eyes of the mouse to prevent drying.
Make a 1-cm-long skin incision and ligate the femoral artery and its branches with 5-10 silk sutures, then excise.
Inject indocyanine green (ICG) (0.1 mL of 100 µg/mL) through the tail vein to monitor blood flow.
Perform ICG fluorescence imaging using a fluorescence imaging system in the reflectance geometry.
Intramuscularly inject microtissues into three sites of the gracilis muscle around the artery incision using a 1 mL syringe with a 23-gauge needle.
Keep the mouse warm with a heated pad in the recovery cage after surgery.
Inject subcutaneously meloxicam to relieve pain after surgery.
Monitor continuously until the mouse is awake.
Monitor therapeutic efficacy of 3D microtissue-treated limb by fluorescence imaging after 28 days.
Inject subcutaneously meloxicam when the mouse shows spontaneous limb amputation to relieve pain.
Euthanize mice with carbon dioxide after completion of experiments.
Wash the microcryogel array chip with 50 mL 0.1 M NaBH4 to quench any residual aldehyde uncross-linked.
Rinse the microcryogel array chip repeatedly with 50 mL deionized water for 3 times, each time for 2 h.
Discard the water after rinsing.
Freeze the microcryogel array chip at -20 °C for 4 to 16 h before lyophilizing according to step 1.2.7.
Modify the 384-multi-well array design to contain 16 × 24 wells, each of 3 mm diameter and 4.5 mm center-to-center spacing.
Remove one side of the backing from a sheet of ultra-thin (10 µm) biocompatible double-sided adhesive tape.
Paste the adhesive tape to one side of a piece of 3-mm-thick PMMA sheet.
Laser engrave the design onto this 3-mm-thick PMMA sheet according to section 1.1.
Align the microcryogel array chip with the reservoir array chip and adhere together tightly to assemble the 3D microcryogel array chip for on-chip cell culture.
Sterilize the assembled 3D microcryogel array chips by ultra-violet radiation for 1 h.
Store 3D microcryogel array chips in vacuum at room temperature for further experiments.
Fill up a wet box with 25 mL sterile de-ionized water to serve as a humidity chamber for cell culture.
Pre-heat the humidified wet box in a 5% CO2 incubator to 37 °C.
Harvest non-small-cell lung cancer cells (NCI-H460) and hepatocellular carcinoma cells (HepG2) from tissue culture plates according to standard protocol.
Re-suspend harvested cells in culture media to a final density of 1.0 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Mix the cell suspension thoroughly.
Remove the humidity chamber from incubator.
Place the assembled 3D microcryogel array chip in the humidity chamber carefully using tweezers.
Mix the cell suspension thoroughly.
Aliquot 3 μL of cell suspension directly onto each microcryogel well.
Lightly touch the pipette tip to the surface before expelling cell suspension.
Add 10 μL of media to each well after cells are seeded into microcryogel using multi-channel pipette.
Culture the cell-loaded microcryogel array chip in the humidity chamber for 24 h at 37 °C with humidified 5% CO2.
Dissolve doxorubicin and IMMLG-84399 in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to form a stock solution of 10 mM.
Dilute drugs with culture medium to form a concentration gradient from 2 nM to 200 µM.
Add 10 µL of drug solutions into each well.
Use 0.1% DMSO diluted in medium as the control.
Incubate the drug-loaded 3D microtissue array in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator at 70 °C for 24 h.
Add 4 µL of resazurin stock solution to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.
Place the 3D microtissue array in the microplate reader.
Detect fluorescence of resazurin metabolized by viable cells at an excitation light wavelength of 560 nm and emission light wavelength of 590 nm.
Subtract the resazurin baseline signal from all wells before further data processing.
Calculate the cell viability fraction of each well by dividing its fluorescence signal by the average fluorescence signal of the control wells.
Plot the dose-response curve in plotting software with the cell viability fraction as the Y-axis and the base 10 logarithm of drug concentration as the X-axis.
Interpolate the 50% inhibition concentration (IC50) at the cell viability fraction of 0.5.
